items.title: Lee Collins Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: The interviewee (Lee Collins) does not speak in the provided transcript. The mention of Janice is in the [INTERVIEWER]'s turn: '...in the joints in Storyville where Janice sat and played...'. The interviewee only responds with a question about a different person ('him').

ctx.x: When he tried to copy, he stole his jelly piece of him and he was a finger buster. He couldn't even play it. He put his name down and composed it. He used to play with Sidney Bichet. I don't know how to really hurt him, I guess, in New York, out on Long Island. They played with Sidney Bichet. I don't know who else. I don't know. Maybe.

I put one line in there. It got a part in there about they didn't know how to wear their pegs. I told him, I said, in the joints in Storyville where Janice sat and played, I said, you couldn't even come in the joint because they didn't find out how much lying you was. Did you ever hear him play down here at all? No, no. See, before he died, about eight months before he died, I lived with him and his wife for nine months in New York. I never knew him before, but when I went to New York, I made a point in my mind…
Did you get along with him all right?
